design:
## Design tests

The refined visuals and the new placement rules were then read blind in seven whole test scenes among other events (`vision/design_tests_v020.md`), the four templates the v0.19 gate failed put in them: the bucket hat in three (once at the back of the park), a drink on a park bench, the dropped ice cream in three with no ice-cream eater beside it, and a jumper in three with a bird nearby. The bucket hat read as a bucket worn as a hat in all three; the drink as "a red cup with a straw"; no jumper was read as reaching for a bird, and no dropped ice cream shared a picture with another cone. The frying pan read as a frying pan with no watering can near it, the standing wheelbarrow and the hose drew no remark, and the blown swing seat, now inside its frame, read as moved by the wind "or just how it was drawn".

Two remarks led to changes before the set was built: two runners ran at someone off their line (a man's feet on a bench 115 px behind it, a jumping girl in the air above it), so a runner's lane is now longer and deeper; and a ladder whose feet stood just behind a bench "could also be read as propped on ... the bench", so the ladder keeps clear of the bench.
intro: All four templates that failed the v0.19 gate pass the seventeenth screen in full: the silver pail read as "an upside-down metal bucket on his head like a hat" in all three of its pictures, at the back of the playground too; the cup with its straw as "drinking from a red cup through a straw" in all three; the ice-cream eater, never beside a dropped ice cream, as eating; and no jumper as reaching for a bird. For the first time all 64 templates pass the gate. No item in any of the 65 pictures was misread or missed outright: 744 of 746 scored items had full marks and two had half points, the fewest of any screen. The set scored 0.998 over all items (0.989 in v0.19), and its unintended oddities fell from 1.3 to 1.2 per picture. `vision/flaws_v020.md` lists the small oddities left for v0.21.
screen: Across all 65 pictures only 2 of 746 scored items fell short of full marks (10 of 760 in v0.19), both by half a point, and none was misread. In the set the one half point was in the tier-4 street, where the girl with the empty cone beside the dropped ice cream was "crying" over "a dropped ice cream" but not said to have dropped it; in a probe the square-wheeled wheelbarrow was offered two readings, "a square wheel ... or a normal round wheel inside a square frame". Two of the three scorers gave no half point at all; the third listed seven hedged items it credited in full. Unintended oddities fell from 27 to 26 in the set and rose from 52 to 68 in the probes, almost all small. None of the v0.19 oddities came back as reported then: no spare watering can beside the pan, no flat wheelbarrow, no swing through its frame, no hole on the path, no ladder over the pond, no foot on the sandpit frame, no runner beside the dropped ice cream. What the readers noticed instead: a worker in a hi-vis vest painting or pointing in a home garden (three probes); a dog bowl far from any dog (five pictures); a shirt on the washing line behind a head read as part of the clothes (three probes); a can with an unused hose reel beside it, or a hose with an unused can (three probes); figures by the pond's cattails; a reading man and a dog walker overlapping in the tier-4 street; seesaws tilted only a little; and the older ones (a stall with nobody at it, goats, leaves under no tree, the bicycle standing on its own).
redrawn: The four v0.19 failures pass at 1.00, the bucket hat over nine items in three pictures. The frying pan, its stream now ending inside the flower bed and no watering can near it, rose from 0.944 to 1.00, every reader naming a frying pan. The dropped ice cream read in full in three of its four pictures, the fourth missing half a point for not saying whose it was. The watering, the hose, the ladder (clear of the pond and the bench), the dig (clear of the path), the runner (with its longer lane), the windy hat and the dog at the door (never with the bench in front of it) all read with full marks.
gate: Every template was screened in at least three pictures (51 in three, 10 in four, 1 in five, 2 in six), and all 64 pass, for the first time. Two passed with a half point: the dropped ice cream (0.969 over 16 items) and the square-wheeled wheelbarrow (0.944 over 9), which read in full in v0.19. About five templates of the gate's movement between screens is reader variance (the v0.9 retest), so a full pass is not a guarantee that other readers would pass every template; it does say that none of the 64 has a cause in its pictures left to fix.
inspection: Inspecting every picture of the set and the probes found nothing new to fix.
